additional_info.subject: Solicitação de Assistência Técnica – Carregador SN Y2R4 313020197007
additional_info.body:
Prezados,
Segue o histórico do problema identificado no carregador SN Y2R4 313020197007, que se encontra atualmente indisponível e inoperante, mesmo após procedimentos realizados em campo:
Histórico do problema:
Data: 03/01/2025.
O carregador ficou indisponível na plataforma OCPP.
Verificamos pela telemetria que toda a infraestrutura elétrica estava operacional, mas o carregador encontrava-se desligado.
Procedimentos realizados:
Ao abrir o carregador, constatamos que o disjuntor DR FB2 estava desarmado (foto 01).
As tensões de alimentação foram medidas e estavam normais.
Rearmamos o FB2 e tentamos ligar os fusíveis FC12 a FC17, mas eles não ligaram.
Observações adicionais:
Foi verificado que a fonte TB17 estava com as luzes de indicação apagadas.
Medimos a alimentação AC da entrada da fonte TB17, que estava normal, mas a saída DC (24V) apresentava 0V.
Testes realizados em campo:
Todos os disjuntores FB3, FC18, FC20, FC21, FC22, FB2 e FC23 estão armados (foto 04).
As luzes indicadoras dos fusíveis QA28, QA29, QA30, QA31, QA32, QA33, QA34 e QA35 estão apagadas (foto 02)
As luzes dos fusíveis FC12, FC13, FC14, FC15, FC16 e FC17 permanecem apagadas, mesmo após tentativa de acionamento via botão (foto 03).
Medições de tensão:
Barramento de entrada principal: OK (vídeo 01).
Saída do disjuntor FB2: OK.
Entrada AC da fonte 24V (TB17): OK (vídeo 02).
Saída DC (24V) da fonte 24V (TB17): 0VDC.
Solicitação:
Dado que todos os procedimentos possíveis em campo foram realizados sem sucesso, solicitamos o envio de um técnico ao local para realizar a análise e correção do problema.
Aguardo retorno para agendamento.
Att.

additional_info.subject: Reported Issue
additional_info.body:
Here is the history of the problem identified in the SN Y2R4 charger 313020197007, which is currently unavailable and inoperative, even after procedures performed in the field:
History of the problem:
Date: 01/03/2025.
The charger became unavailable on the OCPP platform.
We verified through telemetry that the entire electrical infrastructure was operational, but the charger was turned off.
Procedures performed:
When opening the charger, we found that the DR FB2 circuit breaker was tripped (photo 01).
The power supply voltages were measured and were normal.
We reset the FB2 and tried to connect the fuses FC12 to FC17, but they did not turn on.
Additional observations:
It was verified that the TB17 source had its indicator lights off.
We measured the AC power supply from the TB17 source input, which was normal, but the DC output (24V) showed 0V.
Tests performed in the field:
All circuit breakers FB3, FC18, FC20, FC21, FC22, FB2 and FC23 are armed (photo 04).
The indicator lights of fuses QA28, QA29, QA30, QA31, QA32, QA33, QA34 and QA35 are off (photo 02).
The lights of fuses FC12, FC13, FC14, FC15, FC16 and FC17 remain off, even after attempting to activate them via the button (photo 03).
Voltage measurements:
Main input bus: OK (video 01).
Circuit breaker output FB2: OK.
AC input of the 24V source (TB17): OK (video 02).
DC output (24V) of the 24V source (TB17): 0VDC.
Request:
Since all possible procedures in the field were unsuccessful, we request that a technician be sent to the site to analyze and correct the problem.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0398265-DC/Si-D/BR-[oT2t3G] Charger Out of Order CRM:00798001658
additional_info.body:
Hi Joao,
We need to plan for the Site Intervention.
We have analysed the Charger over ther period of 1Week.
We have following error flags.
AUTOM_TempHumiSensor
44
AUTOM_PT1000
21
SECC_GeneralData_MB_Problem
19
INC_PT1000
9
Firstly, We need to check if QA25 is tripped.
Also, Upon further investigation of logs, We see following:
PLC-Error-Flag 'AUTOM_TempHumiSensor' changed to true - (VIN:0 CRE:0 CSM:0 SCE:0 SRI:0 ORI:0 OHW:1 OHS:0 OHSe:0 ST:T)
PLC-Error-Flag 'AUTOM_PT1000' changed to true - (VIN:0 CRE:0 CSM:0 SCE:0 SRI:0 ORI:0 OHW:1 OHS:0 OHSe:0 ST:T)
"OHW:" → sensor reading is above the overheat warning
Then, We need to investigate the resistance of the Temperature sensor.  It Should as per the PT1000
For investigating BT1 & BT2, We need to check the voltage between (I2 and Ground) and it should be comparable between (I8 and Ground)
Similarly, We need to check the voltage between (I1 and Ground) and it should be comparable between (I7 and Ground)
Also, LOGO is on FW v2.6.0, We need to update the LOGO to v2.7.0.
Charger FW is on v2.5.9.4,
Once charger is in Healthy state, We recommend the Charger at Latest FW v6.0.3.
Do let us know, if you have any other query.
Also, If you need assistance in the site intervention.
Thank and Best Regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Giridhar "Gary"

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0398265-DC/Si-D/BR-[oT2t3G] Charger Out of Order CRM:00798001658
additional_info.body:
Hi Joao,
Thanks for connecting over teams and raising queries.
FW update
Since the charger is on
v2.5.9.4-0-g282b68e, Once Charger is online, You need to update the Charger to v2.11 via OTA (from SCB)
Let us know if needed assistance in updating FW via OTA.
And latest FW is v6.0.3, We recommend charger to be on latest FW.
We need to update the Charger FW from v2.11 -→ v3.2.8 -→ v4.0.11 -→ v5.0.23 -→ v6.0.3.
No need to go for the USB update. as after v2.5.9; OTA update is possible.
2. PT1000 Resistance Table
Ambient Temp vs Resistance value is shown in Table.
3. We need to ensure the Charger have data atleast  ~8 GB  for FW update.
Do let us know if you need assistance in site intervention.
if So, Do let us know in advance.
Thank and Best Regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Giridhar "Gary"
